name: Ammihud
title: Ephraimite ancestor and father of tribal leader Elishama
summary: Ammihud belonged to the tribe of Ephraim and is primarily known in the biblical narrative as the father of Elishama, who led the tribe of Ephraim during the wilderness journey after leaving Egypt. Through Elishama, Ammihud is connected to central events such as the census, the organization of Israel's camp, and the consecration of the tabernacle altar, as recorded in Numbers. In the genealogy in 1 Chronicles, an Ammihud is also listed in the direct lineage from Ephraim down to Joshua son of Nun—one of Israel's most prominent leaders. Whether this Ammihud is identical to Elishama's father is debated, but the connection nonetheless gives the name Ammihud an important place in the tribal history of Ephraim and in the broader narrative of Israel's leadership during the wilderness period.

versions.summary: Ammihud was the father of Elishama, who served as leader of the tribe of Ephraim during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness. He is mentioned in several genealogies and in connection with the organization of the tribes of Israel during their departure from Egypt. Ammihud is also noted as an ancestor in the lineage leading to Joshua son of Nun.

The title should be adjusted to avoid confusion.; [major] Ammihud is not described as a 'leader' in the Bible. It is his son Elishama who was the leader of the tribe of Ephraim. Ammihud is mentioned primarily as the father of Elishama and as an ancestor in the genealogy of Ephraim. The role should be changed to something more precise, such as 'patriarch' or 'ancestor'.; [minor] The summary states that Ammihud is 'an ancestor in the lineage leading to Joshua son of Nun'. According to 1 Chron 7:26-27, Ammihud appears in Ephraim's genealogy leading to Joshua through Elishama and Nun, but it should be clarified that this refers to a specific Ammihud in the Chronicles genealogies, as there is debate over whether it is the same person. Otherwise, the summary is good.; [minor] According to 1 Chron 7:26, Ammihud was the son of Laadan (or Tahath in other genealogical lists). The father field should be filled where biblical basis exists.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. Information should be added about the meaning of the name, the possible different individuals named Ammihud in the Old Testament, and the connection of this lineage to Joshua.

Ammihud is mentioned repeatedly in Numbers in connection with his son's role in the census, the arrangement of the camp, and the consecration of the tabernacle altar. In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles, Ammihud is also placed in the lineage from Ephraim down to Joshua son of Nun, giving him a significant place in the history of the tribe of Ephraim.
versions.title: Ephraimite ancestor and father of tribal leader Elishama
versions.reason: [major] According to 1 Chr 7:26, Ammihud is the son of Elishama (in the lineage Ephraim → ... → Elishama → Ammihud → Elisjama → Nun → Joshua). The current value 'laadam' (Laadam) is not correctly identified as the father of this Ammihud. Laadam is mentioned in 1 Chr 7:26 as another person in the line, but the direct father of Ammihud in this text is Elishama. Note however that the genealogy in 1 Chr 7:25-27 is disputed and varies between manuscripts. Some read the sequence so that the father's name is Elishama, while others read it differently. In any case, 'laadam' is not given as the direct father of Ammihud in any standard reading.; [minor] The summary is good, but to distinguish itself more from version 1 and provide greater depth, one could highlight Ammihud's place in Joshua's lineage more clearly and offer a broader contextualization of his role in the tribal history of Ephraim.; [minor] The role 'patriarch' is somewhat generic. The second footnote should perhaps be categorized as 'linguistic' or 'historical' rather than 'theological', since it primarily deals with name similarity and identification of different persons, not a theological question in itself.

footnotes.text: The name Ammihud (עַמִּיהוּד) means 'my people are majestic' or 'my people are glorious' in Hebrew, composed of 'ammi' (עַמִּי, my people) and 'hud' (הוּד, majesty/glory). The name expresses praise for the greatness of the people, a common pattern in Hebrew naming.

There are several individuals named Ammihud in the Old Testament: father of Elishama from Ephraim (Num 1:10), father of Shemuel from Simeon (Num 34:20), father of Pedahel from Naphtali (Num 34:28), father of Talmai, king of Geshur (2 Sam 13:37), and a person mentioned in 1 Chron 9:4. Whether any of these references point to the same person is debated among scholars.

The genealogy in 1 Chron 7:25-27 places Ammihud in the direct line from Ephraim down to Joshua son of Nun. This genealogy is one of very few texts that reconstruct Joshua's full lineage, making Ammihud a key figure in this tribal tradition.

The tribe of Ephraim held a prominent political and military position among the Israelites. The fact that Elishama son of Ammihud was appointed as tribal leader already at the first census after the departure from Egypt testifies to the family's high status within the tribe.

The lineage in 1 Chron 7:25-27 contains several textual-critical challenges. The order and identification of names vary across different manuscript traditions, and there is disagreement among scholars about the exact father-son relationships for several of the individuals mentioned, including Ammihud.

In rabbinic tradition, the lineage of the tribe of Ephraim holds special significance because it leads to Joshua, Moses' successor who led the Israelites into the promised land. Ammihud as a link in this chain underscores the tribe's leading role in Israelite tradition.
